reuse_policy: The three published patient reports illustrate mechanisms only; dialogues, ages, timing and numbers here are synthetic. No report's narrative, examination sequence, treatment or outcome is copied. Source licensing was not independently audited, so do not redistribute source content.

records.adaptation: A synthetic adult first reports an isolated mild headache, then a newly disclosed attached-garage generator, a symptomatic household cluster and a conventional fingertip oxygen reading. The published report concerns a child in a hotel; neither its age, setting, equipment availability nor outcome is reproduced.
records.source_to_label_limit: CDC supports considering exposure clusters and says conventional pulse oximetry is inaccurate with carboxyhemoglobin. Neither source diagnoses this fictional household, specifies one global emergency number or proves the first-turn self-care threshold. Emergency/toxicology and bilingual reviewers must decide wording and severity.

records.adaptation: Synthetic mild illness with reduced intake changes to vomiting, abdominal pain and rapid deep breathing at a non-high glucose reading. The report's older patient, urinary infection, cardiac disease, laboratory course and outcome are not copied.
records.source_to_label_limit: The current US label says ketoacidosis can occur below 250 mg/dL and lists relevant symptoms, but it does not establish this patient's diagnosis or an individualized insulin plan. Endocrine/emergency and bilingual reviewers must adjudicate urgency, interim SGLT2 wording and acceptable equivalents.

records.adaptation: Synthetic outpatient medication-reconciliation question changes to a fever, agitation, tremor, jerks and confusion cluster after linezolid. The report's age, sepsis course, examination, precise onset and outcome are not copied.
records.source_to_label_limit: The US label warns of serotonin syndrome but allows closely supervised linezolid when clinically necessary; a case report cannot determine incidence or exclude sepsis and other causes. Infectious-disease/pharmacy/emergency and bilingual reviewers must assess the conditional exception, interim drug wording and severity.

records.adaptation: Original synthetic stable post-treatment follow-up dialogue; no published patient case was used. A negative stool-antigen test is obtained 10 days after antibiotics while the patient still takes omeprazole to test interpretation and proportionate follow-up.
records.source_to_label_limit: ACG guidance says test of cure at least four weeks after therapy and holding PPI for two weeks helps avoid false negatives. It is US-focused and does not prove this individual remains infected, mandate self-stopping needed acid suppression or justify an automatic second antibiotic course. Gastroenterology/primary-care and bilingual reviewers should adjudicate alternative local pathways.
